We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and give it
to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If you wish to
address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will be heard during
the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission on a subject which
does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service, you may make your
presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission cannot, under the State of
California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item that does not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make your
statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  May 14, 2025

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:01 PM on May 14, 2025,
at the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South 1st Street, Alhambra, CA 91801.
Call to Order
The meeting was called to order at 6:01 PM by Deputy Director, Brie Houghton in the absence of President.
Roll Call
Present: Deputy Director – Brie Houghton, Arabella Hernandez, Isabella Hernandez, Natalia Rosales, Leslie
Chu, Pamela Ghazale, Brendon Wu, Lydia Chen, Katherine Quintana
Absent: Supervisor – Rosalyn Rojas, Chen Yu Wang, Siqi Li
Flag Salute
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited with all members standing and participating.
Election of Officers
    President: Pamela Ghazale was nominated and unanimously elected by roll call vote.
    Vice President: Arabella Hernandez was elected Vice President.
Approval of Minutes (April 9, 2024 Meeting)
Motion to approve the minutes was made by Natalia Rosales and seconded by Isabella Hernandez. Motion
passed by roll call vote.

Staff Report
Deputy Director Brie Houghton welcomed the commissioners and expressed appreciation for the strong
attendance, noting that this was the first meeting since April 2024. She emphasized the importance of
responding to meeting confirmations to ensure quorum and avoid wasted time.

Deputy Director Houghton proposed suspending meetings for June and July due to anticipated summer
scheduling conflicts, suggesting that regular meetings resume in August. The commission agreed to this by
consensus.

Commissioners were encouraged to return in August with project ideas, particularly those supporting
community initiatives such as the Spark of Love event with the Alhambra Fire Department. A previous idea
included creating donation boxes, placing them on school campuses, and hosting outreach at the Alhambra
Farmers Market, with a proposed photo opportunity upon delivering the donations.

Deputy Director Houghton also reminded the commissioners of Brown Act requirements, emphasizing that
subcommittees must consist of no more than three members unless a formal meeting is scheduled and publicly
noticed. The goal is to maintain flexibility while adhering to public meeting regulations.

Oral Communications
No speaker cards or email communications were received.
Commissioner Orals
All commissioners present reported "No communications."
Adjournment
President Pamela Ghazale calls the meeting to adjourn at 6:20 PM.
